CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male who presents with an upper respiratory infection. He reports that approximately one week ago, while doing yard work and landscaping, he started to feel tired and short of breath. He attributes the illness to his first cold of the season, as he was not wearing masks at the end of summer. He reports that the shortness of breath occurred primarily with exertion, specifically when lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil. He denies coughing up sputum at this time but feels it may develop. He reports feeling a little warm but attributed this to exertion rather than fever. He endorses elbow and knee pain, which he associates with the heavy lifting during landscaping. He denies nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies seasonal allergies. Denies nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Positive for fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion, elbow and knee pain, and feeling warm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type two diabetes, hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (to be increased), lisinopril 20 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works during the week. Engages in yard work and landscaping. Participates in barre classes for relaxation. Monitors blood sugar and blood pressure during work week but not consistently on weekends. Diet generally good with occasional indulgences at social gatherings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, no fever. Heart sounds strong and regular. Scattered rhonchi bilaterally on lung exam, clears with cough. Mild edema of lower extremities noted. Pain to palpation of elbows bilaterally.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia. Hemoglobin A1C: 8 (elevated; goal 6-7).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/viral syndrome: COVID test to be sent. Advised symptomatic management with Robitussin for cough and ibuprofen or Tylenol for fever. Anticipated resolution in a couple of days.
2. Depression: Patient reports doing well with current non-medication management including barre classes. Offered option of medication or psychotherapy; patient prefers to reassess in a few months.
3. Type two diabetes: Metformin increased to 1000 milligrams twice daily. Hemoglobin A1C to be rechecked in four months.
4. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled. Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered.
Follow-up appointment scheduled in four months. Patient instructed to report if symptoms worsen.
